Scope addition · 2026-11-08T03:23Z

A third pre-existing `columnMap` miss joins this card. The #31328 thread measured it live on Oracle. A paged read of a federated object gets no unique tie-breaker, even when `columnMap` names the key column. On Oracle, every PAGINATION walk repeated some rows and lost others. SQLite hides it behind rowid order. On PostgreSQL and MySQL, a non-unique sort can do the same, silently.

- [ ] A paged read of an external object whose `columnMap` maps the key appends the mapped key as the final `ORDER BY` tie-breaker. An object with no mapped key is unchanged.
- [ ] A sqlite pin that is red before the fix.
- [ ] Its own patch changeset.

The fix exists as a self-contained commit on the #31328 branch: `e7935cd813bf61000801e531b903c310e8824f0e`. Port it onto main. Do not cherry-pick it blindly; strip anything Oracle-specific.
